newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - T-BOND VOLS SOFT AS FUTURES CONSOLIDATE.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - T-BOND VOLS SOFT AS FUTURES CONSOLIDATE.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. Treasury bond options were steady to lower Wednesday as the underlying futures continued to trade sideways.

Floor traders said activity in options was relatively subdued, mirroring the tone in futures. A handful of put purchases stood out, as traders observed the tendency recently has been to buy puts to hedge long positions in futures.
September implied volatility was pegged at 7.40 percent at the close, down from about 7.55 percent at the previous day's settlement, according to one trading desk.

Volatility in bond options has a history of trending lower in early August, reflecting the summer holiday season in the U.S. and overseas, one analyst noted. He said his research showed bond volatility declining in nine of the past 10 years in the periods from late July to mid-August.
Futures ended 5/32 higher at 114-24/32, bouncing back slightly after matching the previous session low of 114-10/32.
The market's inability to either extend Friday's severe pullback or resume the larger uptrend was also capping volatility, traders said.

One dealer firm bought 5,000 September 114-00 puts and a second dealer bought 3,000 December 112-00 puts. Another dealer sold 1,000 September 115-00 calls and a U.S. bank sold 2,000 December 112-00 puts.
In Eurodollar options, December at-the-money straddle volatility slipped 0.2 percentage point to 9.3 percent, while March was steady at 11.0 percent.
